release_summary.summary: The problem is that recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced incorrect bill calculations, causing a surge in dispute tickets despite most disputed bills being based on actual reads. This was established by observing the dispute ticket volume rise from ~600 per month in June‑July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September (E-03), seeing that actual‑read disputed bills outnumber estimated‑read disputed bills (E-04), confirming the tariff change log shows no tariff changes this year (E-05), noting the billing import validation rule change log contains recent modifications that affect bill calculation (A-01), and finding that 1,184 disputed estimated bills had AMI reads before cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption, indicating rule‑based rejections (E-12). The released item is the minimum useful scope of monitoring dispute volume (action monitor_dispute_volume on DA‑TICKET) as defined in the solution design, together with packaging and submission work items and pending release‑blocking verification. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the verification obligation VOB‑U‑01 (whether the recent rule changes produce incorrect calculations) is resolved, assumptions are active, all constraints are satisfied, the gate result is CONDITIONAL_PASS, and known limitations are documented. Known limitations are that the gate was conditionally passed with deferred items tracked as VOBs and that unfinished work labeled BRIDGE remains (multiple instances).

output.summary: The problem is that recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced incorrect bill calculations, causing a surge in dispute tickets despite most disputed bills being based on actual reads. This was established by observing the dispute ticket volume rise from ~600 per month in June‑July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September (E-03), seeing that actual‑read disputed bills outnumber estimated‑read disputed bills (E-04), confirming the tariff change log shows no tariff changes this year (E-05), noting the billing import validation rule change log contains recent modifications that affect bill calculation (A-01), and finding that 1,184 disputed estimated bills had AMI reads before cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption, indicating rule‑based rejections (E-12). The released item is the minimum useful scope of monitoring dispute volume (action monitor_dispute_volume on DA‑TICKET) as defined in the solution design, together with packaging and submission work items and pending release‑blocking verification. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the verification obligation VOB‑U‑01 (whether the recent rule changes produce incorrect calculations) is resolved, assumptions are active, all constraints are satisfied, the gate result is CONDITIONAL_PASS, and known limitations are documented. Known limitations are that the gate was conditionally passed with deferred items tracked as VOBs and that unfinished work labeled BRIDGE remains (multiple instances).
